description: Metered: one Engine API call. Cut rectangular parts from sheets (panels, plywood, glass, sheet metal) and get the layout, cut plan and yield. 2D panel optimization. Nest rectangular parts into rectangular sheets. Returns the placement of every part, the remaining offcuts, the guillotine cut plan and the yield metrics. Parts named in `matchedSets` (grain matching) are cut side by side from one piece of board, one kerf apart; each placed member says which set and position it is.

engine.description: Which optimizer to run. `heuristic` is the guillotine multi-strategy packer: highest yield, every layout edge-to-edge saw-cuttable, always a full `cutPlan`. `balanced` is a MaxRects free-nesting packer: much faster on large jobs for a small yield cost, but its layouts are often not guillotine (`guillotineValid: false`, `cutPlan: null`), and it does not model `tolerance`, `minimizeCost`, `grainGroup`, `maxCutStages` or `minimizeRotations` — set one of those and a string in `warnings` tells you it was ignored. `max` is the ASYNCHRONOUS tree-search tier (2D only): it reaches the proven optimum on far more jobs at the cost of seconds-to-a-minute per solve, so instead of a plan it returns **202** with a `jobId` — poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` for the result. Still deterministic and guillotine-valid. Where the tier is not enabled on a deployment, `engine: "max"` fails closed with **503**. **What `max` models.** It packs ONE stock format at full sheet size with unlimited supply and a fixed 3-stage guillotine pattern. Anything that would make the returned plan physically WRONG is therefore REFUSED with **400** at submission — before a call is reserved and before you wait for the solve: a second `stock` row, `options.trim`, `options.respectStock`, any `material`, any `grainGroup`, a non-empty `matchedSets` (an empty one is fine). Options that only make the plan less tuned are accepted and listed in `warnings`: `tolerance`, `minimizeCost`, `maxCutStages` (fixed at 3), `minimizeRotations`, `firstCut`, `effort`. A `max` result reports no `offcuts`. Send those jobs to `heuristic`. The default never changes silently.

include.description: Three kinds of token. NARROWING (`cutPlan`, `offcuts`): omit the field entirely to get both; a present array keeps only the narrowing tokens it lists (an empty array drops both). ADDITIVE EXPORT (`svg`, `csv`, `dxf`): each adds an inline export STRING to the response (`svg` a standalone 2D layout — 2D only, a warning is returned for 1D/wood; `dxf` an R12/AC1009 drawing; `csv` a cut list, RFC 4180 quoted (a part name with a comma or a quote stays one field) and formula-injection-guarded (a name beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR is prefixed with an apostrophe so a spreadsheet reads it as text, not a formula — CWE-1236). 2D DATA (`labels`, `planHash`, `pdf`, `labelsPdf`): `labels` adds per-piece label data (`labels[]`, see `Label2D`), `planHash` a 64-hex fingerprint of the plan (the same plan always gives the same hash), `pdf` the cutting-plan PDF and `labelsPdf` the label PDF, both base64-encoded and drawn by the same code as the CutOptim app. These four are 2D only: a 1D or wood request returns a `warnings` entry instead. `pdf` renders at most 500 parts (total quantity); a larger 2D request with `pdf` is a 413 `too_large` with `details.path: "include"`. Export and data tokens do not affect narrowing, so `["svg"]` adds svg and — listing no narrowing token — drops cutPlan/offcuts; use `["cutPlan","offcuts","svg"]` to keep everything.

matchedSets.description: Matched sets (grain matching): groups of parts cut side by side from one piece of board. Send a NON-EMPTY ARRAY of sets (at most 50); members are named by `parts[].id`. Only a non-empty array switches the feature on: absent, `null`, `[]` — and any value that is not an array — is a request without sets, answered exactly as before (no error). With sets the response adds `sheets[].parts[].matchedSet` on every member and a `matchedSets` rollup; `csv` gains `Set` and `Position` columns at the end, `svg` the `matched-sets` frame group, `dxf` the position code on LABELS; `pdf` and `labelsPdf` draw the members as ordinary parts for now (a `warnings` line says so; the set marks are in `sheets[].parts[].matchedSet`, `csv` and `svg`). Engine `max` refuses a non-empty array (400 `details.unsupported`); an empty one is fine. 2D only: the 1D, wood and nest endpoints ignore this field and `parts[].id`.

items.description: Parts cut out of ONE piece of board, side by side or one above the other, exactly one kerf apart, so the figure of the veneer runs on across them (a drawer front over two doors). The set travels through the optimizer as one rectangle — the block — and comes back as its members. Every refusal is a 400 before the quota is reserved; a size mismatch is a warning (`matchedSets[].warnings`), not an error. At most 24 members per set; a part can be in one set only. Engines `heuristic` and `balanced` (which does not rank `priority`, so under `respectStock` a set can lose its place there); `max` refuses a request with sets (400 `details.unsupported`).

grain.description: The SET's grain: along the block's width (`w`) or height (`h`); it decides the direction of every member (their own `grain` is not used inside the block). Absent/null = no grain: the block may turn when every member is `rotatable`.

id.description: Unique among the sets; at most 64 characters. Echoed on every member placement and in `matchedSets[]` of the response (as a string).

installGap.description: The gap between the members ON THE CABINET (default: the kerf). The `align` check measures the lines with it; on the sheet the members still stand one kerf apart, and when the kerf is wider a `gap:` warning says so. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

layout.description: Where each member sits, as lines of `parts[].id` values. `rows`: each line is a row of members side by side, the rows stacked top to bottom (`[["DF"], ["DOOR", "DOOR"]]` = a drawer front over two doors). `cols`: each line is a column of members one above the other, the columns side by side. A part may appear more than once in one set. Positions are numbered in reading order: top to bottom, left to right.

dir.description: `rows`: each line is a row of members side by side, the rows stacked top to bottom. `cols`: each line is a column, the columns side by side.

lines.description: The members, as `parts[].id` values — `[["DF"], ["DOOR", "DOOR"]]` is a drawer front over two doors.

name.description: Optional label, echoed in the response rollup. Printable characters only.

onMiss.description: When the block fits no stock sheet: `split` places the members one by one (with a warning), `unplaced` lists them in `unplaced`.

qty.description: How many instances (three identical cabinets → 3). The parts' `qty` must cover every instance.

effort.description: Search depth, trading solve time against yield. `balanced` (the default) runs the full multi-strategy best-of. `fast` skips the two expensive refinements — the per-board area-combination search and the tail right-sizing that moves the last boards onto a smaller stock size: markedly faster on large jobs (hundreds of parts) for a small yield cost, while staying guillotine-valid and never denser than `balanced` — its candidate set is a strict subset. On small jobs the two are usually identical. Applies to engine `heuristic`; the `balanced` engine (MaxRects) ignores it.

firstCut.description: Force the orientation of the first cut across the board. `auto` searches both and also enables two extra strategy families that are not direction-aware. Applies to each sheet as sent, also on a `grain` row whose grain runs the other way.

kerf.description: Blade width. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

labels.description: Label settings — the same settings as the Label format panel of the CutOptim app, under these names. They shape `labelsPdf` and add `piece`, `of`, `sheetNo`, `stockRow` and `sheetMeta` to every `labels[]` entry. Every field is optional; `{}` is valid and only adds those fields. Absent: the label PDF is the A4 sheet and `labels[]` is exactly as without this object. Validated STRICTLY, unlike the rest of `options`: an unknown key, a wrong type or a value out of range is a 400 `invalid_request` with `details.path`, before any call is counted (also on `/v1/validate/2d`). `null` for a field means the field is absent. Sent without `include` `labels` or `labelsPdf`, it changes nothing and the answer says so in `warnings`. 2D only.

dimSize.description: Size of the dimension text on the label.

factoryEdges.description: Mark FE on the edges of a piece that lie on a sheet edge with no `trim` on that side (the board's factory edge).

format.description: `sheet` = the A4 sheet of labels (3 columns); `roll` = one label per page, `width` × `height` mm, for a label printer; `apli-03056` = APLI 03056 sheets (24 labels of 64.6 × 33.9 mm on A4, 3 × 8); `brother-dk-11201` = Brother DK-11201 roll labels (29 × 90 mm, one per page).

offset.description: Printer offset in mm: moves everything printed on the label right (`x`) and down (`y`); negative values move it back. Applied rounded to 0.1 mm.

order.description: `input` = labels in `parts` order; `cut` = sheet by sheet, in the order the saw plan frees the pieces.

partNo.description: Print the part number, top left and largest: the 1-based row of the FIRST `parts` row with that name (rows sharing a name share a number; with unique names it equals `labels[].partNo`).

parts.description: Print only the labels of these part numbers (the numbers `partNo` prints), e.g. to re-print after sanding. Empty or absent = all.

stageWords.description: Your own word for a built-in stage key, at most 6 characters; empty or absent = the English abbreviation (RC, C2S, EB, S, D).

stages.description: Work stages printed as a row of circles to tick off by pen; empty or absent = no row. Each entry is a built-in key — `rc` (rough cut), `c2s` (cut to size), `eb` (edge banded, printed only on a banded part), `s` (sanded), `d` (drilled, not printed yet) — or free text of at most 6 characters, printed as sent (keys are lower case: `RC` is free text). Spaces are trimmed; printable characters only.

maxCutStages.description: Panel-saw stage limit — a count of machine PHASES (axis changes), not raw cut-tree depth. A real kitchen job is commonly 9 cuts deep but only 3 stages. An unsatisfiable limit still returns the best plan plus a string in `warnings`; it is never an error.

minOffcut.description: Output filter only: report a leftover rectangle only if its SHORT side is at least this. Does not change the layout.

minimizeCost.description: Rank candidate layouts by total stock price instead of sheet count. Needs `price` on the stock rows to mean anything.

minimizeRotations.description: Prefer layouts that turn fewer parts, at a possible small yield cost.

respectStock.description: Treat each stock row's `qty` as a hard cap. Parts that then do not fit come back in `unplaced` instead of on an extra invented sheet.

setOutlines.description: A boolean. With `matchedSets` and the `svg` export: draw the dashed frame and the "SET A" badge of every set instance, in ONE separate group (`<g id="matched-sets" data-role="annotation">`) a laser or CNC import can drop in one move. `false` leaves that group out (the position codes in the part labels stay). Read only in a request with sets — there a value other than `true`, `false` or `null` is a 400; without sets the field is ignored, whatever it holds.

tolerance.description: Accept a cut that overshoots by up to this much, i.e. allow parts to encroach on the kerf. Turns "two 501 mm parts do not fit a 1000 mm board" into one board.

trim.description: Per-side edge trim removed before nesting. Asymmetric on purpose: a damaged long edge may need more than the others, and a symmetric trim would then give a wrong plan, not merely a worse one. `left` shifts placements right, `top` shifts them down. The sides are those of each sheet as sent — also on a `grain` row whose grain runs the other way.

bottom.description: Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

left.description: Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

right.description: Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

top.description: Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

edgeBanding.description: Per-edge banding. Each side names the banding TYPE as a free-string reference (e.g. `"ABS oak 22×1"`); an absent or empty side is not banded. Library-independent — send your own ERP reference codes and the `edgeBanding` response block groups the metreage by that exact string. Metadata only: it never changes placement, it is summarised post-hoc into linear metres. 2D only.

bottom.description: Type reference for the bottom edge (runs the part width).

left.description: Type reference for the left edge (runs the part height).

right.description: Type reference for the right edge (runs the part height).

top.description: Type reference for the top edge (runs the part width).

grain.description: Grain direction: the side of the part the grain runs along (`w` or `h`). On a sheet whose stock row has a `grain`, the part is placed with its grain along the sheet's, turned 90° when it has to be (`rotated: true` on the placement) — `rotatable` is then ignored for it. With `material`, only boards of the part's own material count. No grained stock → no effect, and `warnings` says so. In a matched set a member's own `grain` is not used: the set's `grain` decides, and a `grain:` line in `matchedSets[].warnings` names the members it overrides.

grainGroup.description: DEPRECATED — still accepted and still working exactly as before. Parts sharing a group are kept on one sheet. If a group is too large for one sheet the members are split and a string in `warnings` names the group. It only keeps them on ONE SHEET: it does not place them next to each other, so it gives no continuous grain across them. For fronts whose figure must run on (a drawer front over two doors) use `matchedSets`.

h.description: Part height. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

id.description: The row's id, so a `matchedSets` layout can name it. Any JSON value is accepted here. Only an id a set REFERS TO is checked: it must be a non-empty string of printable characters, at most 64 long, or a safe integer (`7` and `"7"` are the same id), and it must be on exactly one part. Every other id is ignored, whatever it holds (a float, an object, null, repeated, long, empty): always without a non-empty `matchedSets`, and on the rows no set names with one — so an ERP article number is safe to send.

material.description: Material identity — a HARD placement constraint. A part of material X is cut ONLY from stock of material X (unlike `edgeBanding`, this changes the layout). Free string, library-independent: send your own ERP code. Absent = the "unspecified" partition (matches only material-less stock). With no part or stock carrying `material`, the whole solve is byte-identical to before.

meta.description: Opaque JSON object (any keys) echoed back VERBATIM on the matching output (a part's meta on every placed piece of it; a stock row's meta on every sheet/rod cut from it). Attach ERP article numbers, order-line ids, customer refs to reconcile the cut plan with your system. Never parsed, never affects placement. Part meta follows its request row: the meta of each row lands on exactly its qty of placed pieces, even when rows share a name; stock meta by stock-row order.

name.description: Optional label, echoed on every placement. Defaults to `Part <1-based row index>`.

priority.description: Must-cut. Wins board space over non-priority parts when stock is capped — only meaningful together with `options.respectStock`.

qty.description: How many identical copies. Expanded server-side into individual pieces; the sum across all rows must not exceed 2000.

rotatable.description: May the part be turned 90°? Set false for print-direction parts. For grain, prefer `grain` — it says WHICH side the grain runs along, so the part is turned to match the sheet instead of being frozen in the orientation you happened to send.

w.description: Part width. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

grain.description: Grain direction of this sheet: the side the grain runs along (`w` or `h`). Absent = no grain (MDF, melamine): parts without a `grain` rotate freely on it, while a part WITH a `grain` keeps the orientation the grained rows give it (send `material` to keep grained and plain boards apart). Echoed on every `sheets[]` entry cut from this row. Rows whose grain runs different ways may be mixed; `options.trim` and a forced `options.firstCut` still apply to each sheet in its own row's orientation.

h.description: Sheet height. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

material.description: A stock unit of material X serves only material-X parts. Free string; see the part `material`.

meta.description: Opaque JSON object (any keys) echoed back VERBATIM on the matching output (a part's meta on every placed piece of it; a stock row's meta on every sheet/rod cut from it). Attach ERP article numbers, order-line ids, customer refs to reconcile the cut plan with your system. Never parsed, never affects placement. Part meta follows its request row: the meta of each row lands on exactly its qty of placed pieces, even when rows share a name; stock meta by stock-row order.

priority.description: "Use this stock up first" — a soft preference ranked BELOW sheet/rod count. Steers which format is spent first without spending more of it.

qty.description: How many sheets of this format are available. A HARD cap only when `options.respectStock` is true; otherwise the format is treated as unlimited. The sum across all rows must not exceed 5000.

w.description: Sheet width. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.
